name: Bugcrowd
description: Claims Bugcrowd program URLs. The program page is client-rendered: a plain HTTP GET returns a JavaScript shell, so the generic reader refuses it today and this driver needs its own reader (the platform API or an authenticated session) before intake can succeed.

policy_fetch.notes: Measured 2026-11-20: GET /engagements/<handle> with a browser user-agent returns 200 and ~113 KB, but the text is a JavaScript shell with no scope material (0 occurrences of targets / in-scope strings), and /engagements/<handle>.json answers 406 with every Accept header tried. A non-browser fetch with the default kai user-agent returns ~70 bytes of text, which the intake refuses as unreadable rather than writing an empty contract. Reading a Bugcrowd program therefore requires its own reader: either the platform API with a session, or a rendered fetch.

scope_extraction.notes: Heading hits are candidates for the operator to verify; policy text still wins, and nothing is promoted into scope.txt without an explicit flag.

mandatory_conditions.text: Testing must be performed from a Bugcrowd researcher alias (a @bugcrowdninja.com address); traffic from personal identity leaks the researcher and can void the reward.
Severity is expressed in the platform's VRT taxonomy, so the draft must carry a VRT-style category rather than only a CVSS vector.
